stem: A client is placed on Contact Precautions. Which PPE practice follows current CDC guidance?

options.A: Don a gown and gloves on room entry for interactions that may involve contact with the client or the client's environment, and discard contaminated PPE before leaving the room.
options.B: Wear only a surgical mask on room entry because Contact Precautions are designed primarily for respiratory-droplet exposure.
options.C: Use a fit-tested N95 respirator as the required PPE for every Contact Precautions interaction, even when no airborne pathogen is suspected.
options.D: Enter without gown or gloves and add PPE only after visible contamination occurs during care.

rationale: CDC Contact Precautions guidance directs healthcare personnel to use gloves and a gown for interactions that may involve contact with the patient or the patient's environment, with PPE donned upon room entry and contaminated PPE discarded before exiting. Therefore A is correct. B describes a droplet-focused barrier, C applies an airborne respirator requirement to Contact Precautions, and D delays PPE until after exposure rather than using it prospectively for anticipated contact.
educational_objective: For Contact Precautions, don the indicated gown and gloves upon room entry for anticipated patient or environmental contact and remove/discard contaminated PPE before leaving the room.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_version_date: CDC page dated 2024-04-03; current guidance rechecked 2026-08-17
source_locator: Recommendation details > Use Contact Precautions: use PPE appropriately, including gloves and gown; wear gown and gloves for interactions involving contact with patient/environment; don PPE upon room entry and properly discard before exiting; Droplet and Airborne sections used to adjudicate distractors
source_claim_supported: CDC Contact Precautions include gown and gloves for interactions involving patient or environmental contact, donned on room entry and discarded before exit; masks and N95 respirators are specified under different transmission-based precaution categories.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8/PDF p.12: Apply principles of infection prevention (e.g., hand hygiene, aseptic technique, isolation, sterile technique, universal/standard enhanced barrier precautions); Educate client and staff regarding infection prevention measures

correction_summary: Replaced the original PPE-supply-shortage scenario because the cited CDC page did not directly support the operational claims about obtaining supplies or facility escalation. Rebuilt the item around the CDC's explicit Contact Precautions PPE instructions, with distractors drawn from Droplet/Airborne or delayed-PPE errors. Correct answer remains option A; difficulty remains easy.
